Listen to this article Share Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals is looking to raise about $2.1 billion from its public offering, up from the initial $1.6 billion target, after receiving investor applications worth nearly $4.5 billion. Advertisement Advertisement The proposed 30 percent increase would allow the refinery to offer up to 5.33 billion shares, compared with the original 4.1 billion shares, according to a Reuters report on November 17. The initial offer, priced at N525 per share, was expected to generate approximately N2.15 trillion. However, applications of nearly N6 trillion have pushed the company to consider making more shares available to investors. A senior Dangote executive told Reuters that the refinery intends to increase the offer to the permitted limit, subject to approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The allocation of the additional shares is expected to favour Nigerian investors. Retail subscribers are expected to receive all the shares they requested, while local pension funds are likely to receive allocations close to their applications. Foreign investors are expected to absorb most of the reduction in allocations as the company works to accommodate demand. Investors from South Africa, Botswana and Kenya were among those who subscribed to the offer, with South Africa’s Public Investment Corporation also participating. Advertisement Read also: SEC vows to protect small investors as Dangote Refinery allotment awaits nod The fundraising comes as Dangote prepares to expand the refinery’s capacity from 650,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day over the next five years. The expansion programme is estimated to cost $14.3 billion. Advertisement The increase in the IPO target does not mean Dangote is surrendering control of the business. Aliko Dangote is expected to retain about 83.5 percent ownership after the offering, while the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s stake is projected to fall to approximately 6.5 percent. The refinery had previously raised about $2.5 billion through two private placements involving 7.2 billion shares, according to its IPO prospectus. Advertisement Advertisement For the Nigerian Exchange, the enlarged offer could bring more investors into the refinery’s ownership structure and increase the value of shares available for trading once it is listed. However, the proposed $2.1 billion fundraising is yet to be finalised. The additional shares and revised offer size remain subject to regulatory approval. The refinery is expected to list on the Nigerian Exchange later in November, following the completion of the necessary regulatory and listing processes.
